speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of your skin lesions and tell me exactly where your wrist pain is located?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Lyme_disease_serology
Do you recall seeing a tick bite or developing a red, expanding rash on your skin after your camping trip?

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the Lyme serology is negative, I need to rule out other causes of migratory arthritis. Have you noticed any joint swelling or redness in your left wrist, and have you experienced any recent gastrointestinal or urinary symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The negative Lyme serology and the specific description of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions are highly suggestive of disseminated gonococcal infection. Given your history of sexual activity, I need to confirm this suspicion with further testing.
REQUEST TEST: NAAT_for_Neisseria_gonorrhoeae

speaker: Doctor
text:
The positive NAAT confirms the presence of Neisseria gonorrhoeae, which aligns perfectly with your symptoms of migratory arthritis and characteristic skin lesions.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated gonococcal infection
